fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Rockefeller and Medicine, in Clive's View", "body": "Clive de Carle argues that money, not health, shaped modern medicine. In his telling, Rockefeller, who owned oil and much of the press by the 1920s, found he could make pharmaceuticals from oil and paid schools of homeopathy, acupuncture and herbalism to drop their teaching, and he says England's 1939 Cancer Act then restricted who could treat cancer. He claims the average doctor gets about four hours of health study in five years, and recounts doctors he interviewed describing cover-ups in training and a Harvard professor admitting half the teaching was wrong. Chance calls it a medical mafia and points listeners to James Corbett's documentary Rockefeller Medicine."}, {"title": "Clive on How Modern Food Went Wrong", "body": "Clive describes a world two centuries ago where villages ate fresh, local, seasonal food and supplements were rarely needed. He dates the decline to around 1850, blaming cottonseed and other cooking oils, then processed carbohydrates and sugar, and he links unnatural fats to dementia. He argues that dwarf wheat and glyphosate spraying, rather than gluten itself, explain widespread wheat problems, and calls bread before a meal a restaurant trick to make you hungrier. Chance shares his rule that food not organic and local barely counts as food, says getting used to its cost early makes it easier, and warns that some organic labels trace back to big food companies."}, {"title": "Fulvic Minerals and Magnesium, Clive's Staples", "body": "Clive's two favorite supplements get the longest airing. He describes fulvic minerals as a water extract of soil from a small deposit in the United States he says is around 30 million years old, claims they help cells release toxins and take in trace elements and that they neutralize glyphosate, and warns against mixing them with chlorinated or fluoridated water. If he could recommend only one supplement, he says, it would be magnesium, which he links to cramps, sleep, anxiety and heart function, arguing that calcium lets muscle contract while magnesium lets it relax. He cautions that cheap magnesium oxide works poorly and that most bottles suggest too little."}, {"title": "Everyday Detox and the Colon Cleanse", "body": "Asked about cleansing, Clive says the point today is less a harsh ten day detox than detoxing every day, starting with working bowels, a healthy liver and enough water. He suggests raw vegan eating may suit someone overweight while meat, fish, dairy and eggs build up someone thin, and names vitamin C, charcoal and sulfur-rich foods such as eggs, onions and garlic as his tools against toxins and heavy metals. Chance recalls a colon cleanse with bentonite clay from his early episode Metaphysical Dumps, Clive describes a coconut water, clay and psyllium fast in Thailand, and Chance ties physical lightness to spiritual growth."}, {"title": "The Secret Health Club and Censorship", "body": "Clive explains that around 2014 UK authorities made him take down his YouTube videos, and that he and fellow UK Column contributors saw views fall from about 40,000 to 400, so he moved his material behind a members' club hosted in Iceland. The Secret Health Club, he says, holds concise videos on topics like Tesla era technology and the sounds newborn babies use, with a forum and a USB version coming. He says UK rules bar him from making almost any claims about his products. Chance, who got a YouTube strike over a guest's website containing the word healing, argues health is censored because it is the linchpin of control."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Clive de Carle is an erudite Englishman with an excellent grasp on the essentials of nutrition, supplements, and strategies for staying out of hospitals. With his Secret Health Club, Clive provides pointers for peak performance that "they" don't want you to know. Tune in to hear empowering health philosophy, learn about Vitamin C, Magnesium, Fulvic minerals, Iodine, willpower, and much more!
